raw_response:
I have farmed in Quzhou County for 40 years, so I do not chase complicated ideas. I work from what fits my land, my labor, and my water. Since I have well irrigation and my main system is wheat-maize, I will keep that as the backbone on most of my land because it is the most steady for me. I will put the best part of my land and most of my attention into wheat and summer maize, because they feed the household and give stable cash flow. I will still keep some chili because it brings better cash when the market is decent, but I will not expand it too much because it needs more labor and more pesticide work. I will also keep some cotton, but only on a smaller area, because I know how to grow it and it helps spread risk, even if returns are not always as strong as before. For seed, I will use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps yield and standability. For fertilizer, I will stay moderate rather than extreme, because at my age and with 20 mu, I want dependable output, not unnecessary cost. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water mainly at the key stages and not waste it. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it saves labor and matches how I manage the farm now, but I will plough where I want a cleaner seedbed or better root growth.
